evidence.text: Seasonality on the company's own numbers puts Q1 revenue about $53.3-53.8M against a $52.05M bar (+2 to +3%). The bar, less RSR of ~$25.8M (the July-based $103M run rate / 4, +10% y/y on Q1 FY26's $23.4M), implies equipment of ~$26.3M, only +2% on Q1 FY26's $25.7M. Q4 FY26 equipment was $30.5M (+7.7%), with intrusion +36% and StarLink radio sales +40% y/y and +30% sequentially. Last year's Q4-to-Q1 equipment step (28.3 to 25.7, x0.91) applied to $30.5M gives ~$27.7M.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats have not been reliably bought. Q1 FY26 (2025-11-03) beat revenue by ~5% ($49.2M vs $46.8M) and EPS by $0.04, and the stock went -7.7%. Q2 FY26 (2026-02-02) was a small revenue beat with lock strength: +11.2%. Q3 FY26 (2026-05-04) was revenue in line with an EPS beat plus a litigation charge: -15.2%. Q4 FY26 (2026-08-24) beat $55.8M vs $52.5M: -1.3%. Equipment misses have been punished hardest (2025-02-03, distributor destocking: -26.6%).
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus at $52.05M is +5.9% y/y, below the +10-12% growth of every FY26 quarter, and implies equipment barely growing after a Q4 where radio sales grew 40%. If the market had priced the Q4 equipment exit rate, the bar would sit near $53.5M and the stock would not be 17% off its high with all six analysts at Buy. Caveat: this is my own seasonal arithmetic, not a company number, and Q1 FY26 equipment carried a door-locking surge that makes the comp harder.
evidence.independence: Q1 FY26 comparison numbers come from a different primary document (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/69633/000110465925105432/nssc-20251030xex99d1.htm). StarLink +40% / +30% sequential is from https://www.insidermonkey.com/blog/napcos-nssc-record-quarter-comes-with-a-costly-asterisk-attached-1825271/. Allegion's peer read is filed separately as its own finding.

evidence.text: RSR should print about $25.7-26.0M (+10-11% y/y), inside what the company already signalled with a ~$103M July-based run rate. On the Q4 call the CEO said the radio-sales benefit to RSR becomes more visible in the back half of FY27, so no Q1 acceleration is guided.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: RSR has grown 11-13% steadily and has not been the swing line. The big moves came on equipment and one-offs.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is the company's own guided run rate. The small positive is a possible upside surprise if August-September radio activations lifted the run rate above $103M. The market would see that in the new run-rate number disclosed with the release.
evidence.independence: The back-half-FY27 timing comes from Q4 call coverage summarised in search results (https://www.benzinga.com/news/26/08/61400577/napco-security-techs-q4-2026-earnings-call-complete-transcript, 403 on fetch, snippet only). Shares the Q4 release with finding 1.

evidence.text: Allegion, the largest US commercial door-hardware peer, reported on 2026-10-22, after Napco last spoke. For Q3 2026 (same Jul-Sep quarter) it showed Americas revenue +11.7% (+9.1% organic), Americas non-residential up low double digits organically on volume and price, and a raised full-year organic guide to 5-6%. This points to firm demand in the school, healthcare and institutional door-locking channel that Napco's Marks/Alarm Lock products sell into.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Door-locking strength drove Napco's equipment growth in FY26 and the +11.2% reaction on 2026-02-02 ('electronic locks boost 2Q sales').
evidence.why_not_priced: Napco's consensus has not moved off ~$52M since August despite a peer printing accelerating US non-residential hardware. A priced read-through would show estimate revisions and a stock closer to its high. This is a proxy: Napco has not confirmed the transmission, and its own access-control line fell 13.8% in Q4.
evidence.independence: Independent company and document. Napco's own Q4 door-locking strength points the same way (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000069633/000110465926100077/nssc-20260820xex99d1.htm).

evidence.text: In the FY26 10-K the company says it 'has submitted additional [IEEPA] claims which the Company cannot ensure the probability of collection and therefore, no refund receivable has been recognized related to these claims'. Any of those approved by CBP during Jul-Sep 2026 would land as another gross-margin benefit in Q1 FY27, like the ~600bp / $0.09 EPS benefit in Q4.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q4 FY26 beat carried ~$0.09 of tariff refunds and the stock went -1.3% on the day, then slid to ~$34.5 on insider sales. Refund-lifted EPS was not rewarded.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS of $0.37-0.38 matches the ex-refund run rate (Q4 $0.41 ex-refund in the Benzinga/MarketBeat comparison), so any further refund is outside the bar. As a one-off below the run-rate with no path to guidance, it is worth a fraction of its EPS. evidence.independence: None for the company-specific amount.

evidence.text: On the Q4 call the CFO flagged rising electronic-parts costs tied to data-center demand. Q4 equipment gross margin excluding the refund was roughly 26-27% (37.4% reported less ~11pp of refund on a $30.5M equipment base), about flat with Q1 FY26's 26.0%. Price increases are therefore no longer visibly lifting equipment margin, and Q1 equipment margin could compress.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin has been a swing line: the 2024-11 equipment-margin and sales miss went -14.4% (https://itiger.com/news/2480307668). Equipment margin expansion from price increases supported FY26.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS of $0.37-0.38 on $52M implies operating margins similar to Q1 FY26's. A priced parts squeeze would show in EPS estimates cut below the prior-year rate of growth, which they are not. The CFO comment was qualitative, so the size is small.
evidence.independence: The ex-refund margin arithmetic is from the Q4 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000069633/000110465926100077/nssc-20260820xex99d1.htm) and Pulse 2.0's 55.3% ex-refund total GM (https://pulse2.com/napco-q4-gross-margin-jumps-850-basis-points-but-tariff-refunds-account-for-600-basis-points/).

evidence.text: Access control (Continental/MVP) sales fell 13.8% y/y in Q4 FY26 and 11% for FY26, and the CEO said MVP was not yet a meaningful contributor to recurring revenue. That drag continues into Q1 against the locking and intrusion strength.

evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, since it was disclosed with Q4. The residual is that the low equipment bar in finding 1 may already reflect it, which is why finding 1 is held at +1.0.

evidence.text: NRC daily status reports put PSEG's nuclear units at or near full power through Q3, with no refuelling outage at a PSEG-operated unit. On 2026-07-15 Salem 1, Salem 2, Hope Creek and Peach Bottom 2/3 were all at 100%. On 2026-08-15 Hope Creek was at 88% (a feedwater pump out of service) and Salem was at 100%. On 2026-09-15 Hope Creek was at 98% (condenser leakage), Salem at 100%, and Peach Bottom 2 in coastdown to refuelling. This is against a Q2 capacity factor of 92.0% (93.7% YTD) and a Hope Creek forced outage from Feb to Apr 2026.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nuclear output was cited as a driver of the Q2 2026 Power beat; the stock fell 0.46%. Output beats have not been paid on this name.
evidence.why_not_priced: Three point-in-time snapshots, not a capacity factor. Nobody aggregates NRC daily status into a quarterly output estimate for PEG. Most output is hedged, so even a strong quarter moves Power earnings by cents. If it were priced, it would show as Power estimates above Q2's run-rate, and there is no visible sign either way.

evidence.text: Summer 2026 was extreme in PJM: an all-time peak load on 2026-07-02 (~166-168 GW), real-time prices averaging $348/MWh over July 1-3 against a $64 YTD average, and a PSE&G system peak of 10,446 MW, the highest since 2012. evidence.text: The early-July 2026 storms were, per the company, 'one of the largest restoration efforts in its history': ~380,000 customers, 330+ crews, 7,000+ A/C repairs. The cost and whether it is expensed or deferred were not disclosed on the Q2 call. Any expensed portion lands as Q3 O&M. Management knew of it on 2026-08-04 and still reaffirmed guidance.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior storm-cost surprise found in the baseline's 7 prints.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: management included it when it reaffirmed guidance. The cost was never quantified, and NJ has a deferral precedent for major storms (Sandy: ≥85% deferred). If it were a known hit, Q3 estimates would sit below the +8% YoY that $1.22 implies.
evidence.independence: Q2 call summary: storm discussed operationally, no cost treatment given (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-8-4-public-service-enterprise-group-incorporated-stock/). Same company source as above, so not independent.

evidence.text: PSE&G said it 'anticipates filing by year-end 2026 to update base rates', years ahead of its 2029 requirement. NJ legislation also removes the 50bp RTO transmission adder from January 2027 (~$40m net income a year, ~$0.08/share). Both are into Governor Sherrill's affordability agenda: a January 2026 executive order on rate freezes and bill credits, and PSE&G bills described by Jefferies as the highest in NJ. Rate-case size, ROE ask or timing given on the call could revive political-risk selling.

evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the stock is 14.6% off its high and Truist cut its target on 2026-10-15. Request size and timing are still unknown, and a large ask would be new information. If fully priced, the stock would not have rebounded +9% in 20 days into the print.

evidence.text: On 2026-10-06 Constellation and Google signed a 20-year deal for 890 MW of uprates at 11 PJM reactors in IL, PA and NJ; CEG rose ~12-15% that day. The NJ unit is Salem: PSEG operates it and owns 57%, and the NRC list shows PSEG planning stretch-uprate applications for Salem 1 & 2 in Q2 2027. Canary Media puts Salem's uprate at 97 MW. Whether PSEG's 57% share is contracted, and on what terms, has not been disclosed. Its first chance to speak is the Q3 call, where at Q2 it cited 'the potential to contract our nuclear output under multi-year agreements'.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No PSEG nuclear-contract announcement in the baseline window. At Q2 the CEO said 'I wouldn't say there's inflections' on data-center talks, and the stock fell 0.46%.
evidence.why_not_priced: PSEG has not commented since the deal, and no source ties PSEG's share to it. PEG's +9% over 20 days may partly reflect it. A PSEG-confirmed contract on its own output is not in the price, because the stock would trade nearer the $78 200-day than 14.6% off its high. The most likely outcome is no news, hence the small central size and the wide upside tail.
